ops-broadcast: :loudspeaker: HEADS-UP: We will roll out a tightened egress-filter policy to all control-plane nodes across us-west/us-east on Thu 2026-05-14 02:00-02:30 UTC. This is a configuration-only change (no node reboots) but will briefly reset some upstream connections. Expect short spikes in Grpc p50/p95 while connections re-establish.

ops-broadcast: Why: security posture improvement + remove legacy outbound rules. Rollout plan: canary (2% traffic) -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, 5–10m observation between steps. We will run a controlled traffic-shift to exercise fallback routing and autoscaler behavior.

ops-broadcast: Safety controls: 
- Auto-rollback on >3% global error increase sustained 5m
- Canary in us-west first, route-split flagged to SRE oncall
- Temporary SLO window: we will suspend p99 strict alerts for 30m during each region's 20m window (SRE only).

devon: acked. I'll be oncall and watching the runbook. Who's running the canary traffic-shift? :eyes:

liz: @devon infra-deploy-bot will execute the rollout; SREs should watch the `edge-proxy` and `ingress` dashboards and the fallback counts. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-filter-rollout (note: updated with new thresholds).

anand: Heads-up for product infra — client SDKs with persistent multiplexed connections may see reconnect churn. We should queue a brief client-facing note if metrics show >1% failed requests from our SDKs. Taylor, can support ops craft a 1-line status if needed?

taylor: Yup, happy to prep a status snippet. Suggest: "We’re applying a short security configuration update; you may see transient 5xx/connection errors for <5 minutes — no action required."

devon: Quick technical detail for observers: if you need to simulate the condition locally, you can toggle the filter with:
```
kubectl -n controlplane annotate cm/egress-config rollout-test=true
```
Then `kubectl apply -f egress-config.yaml` to re-sync. Please don't run in prod unless you are oncall.

infra-deploy-bot: Scheduled: egress-filter-rollout job queued for 2026-05-14T02:00:00Z. Canary: node-group cp-usw1-canary, step-delay 600s. Trigger will emit `rollout:start` event to #ops-log.

liz: Proposed rollback triggers (in runbook):
- >3% absolute increase in error rate for 10m
- p99 latency > 2x baseline for 10m
- >1.5x reconnection rate for critical streams for 5m
If any of these fire, deploy-bot will auto-pause and notify #eng-sre and #support.

devon: Plan for post-rollout verification: 
- verify `health-check` success on canary pods
- run `synthetic/regression/ingress-smoke` job
- check fallback counts (should be <= baseline * 1.1)
If all green, proceed to next step.

anand: I'll standby to throttle client SDK retries if we get noisy signals — better to fail fast than to overload fallback paths.

ops-broadcast: Ops note: this is a low-risk security-first change; still please treat it like a canary-sensitive rollout. If you can't be available during the window, mute alerts but share coverage pair.

devon: I'll post a quick pre-rollout ping 10m before and then a post-rollout summary.

liz: Post-rollout checklist: paste the `rollout:status` event, the canary metrics snapshot, and any anomalies. Keep summaries to 1–2 bullets.

ops-broadcast: Thanks all — will post updates to this thread during the rollout. :white_check_mark:
